summary: The note introduces the Standing Rules of the United States Senate, the parliamentary procedures the Senate adopts to govern its proceedings. It states that the Senate's authority to set these rules comes from Article One, Section 5 of the United States Constitution, which allows each House to determine the rules of its proceedings.
one_line: Overview of the Standing Rules of the United States Senate and their constitutional basis in Article One, Section 5.
key_facts: The Standing Rules of the Senate are the parliamentary procedures adopted by the United States Senate to govern its procedure.
The Senate's power to establish its rules derives from Article One, Section 5 of the United States Constitution.
Article One, Section 5 of the United States Constitution states: "Each House may determine the rules of its proceedings..."
